paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: The loss comparison between vanilla Transformer and the proposed SepLLM. SepLLM achieves lower loss different computation costs and different training time consistently.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the comparison of training loss over time between a vanilla Transformer model and the proposed SepLLM model. The x-axis represents training time in seconds, ranging from 0 to 250,000 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 50,000. The y-axis represents loss, ranging from 2.40 to 2.75 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.05. Two lines are plotted: the vanilla model is shown as a solid purple line with diamond markers, and SepLLM is shown as a solid red line with circular markers. Both lines exhibit a decreasing trend in loss as training time increases, starting near 2.75 at 0 seconds and approaching approximately 2.50 by 250,000 seconds. The red SepLLM line consistently remains below the purple vanilla line throughout the training period, indicating lower loss at all measured time points. A green dashed rectangle highlights the region from approximately 200,000 to 250,000 seconds, with an annotation indicating a 1.26× improvement, suggesting that SepLLM achieves a faster convergence or better performance within this timeframe.
